title: Let all be done in love (1 Corinthians 16)
word: Let all be done in love
hookLine: a collection, travel plans, greetings, and a closing: watch, stand fast, be strong, love
tomorrow: what if the worst news feels like a verdict already read?
last: SO RUN · A WAY TO ESCAPE · DISCERN THE BODY

cards: The end of a long call with your grandpa: who's driving Sunday, what time, tell your sister hi, love you, bye. Logistics, then love. Paul ends this letter, a letter full of fights, the same way.
Straight after the great chapter on resurrection comes money: "Now concerning the collection for the saints."
Each of them is to set something aside on the first day of the week, as God has prospered them, so nobody is scrambling when Paul arrives. Then travel plans, who might visit and when, and greetings.
And tucked in the middle, five short commands.

teach.h: WATCH, STAND, BE BRAVE, BE STRONG.
teach.b: The first four: "Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong." Quit you like men is old English for be brave, act like grown-ups. They sound like orders at a city gate.

teach.h: LET ALL BE DONE WITH CHARITY.
teach.b: Then the fifth, right behind them: "Let all your things be done with charity." Charity is the King James word for love, the same Greek word as chapter thirteen: agape. Look back over the week.
This church argued over leaders, food, dinner, gifts, worship and the resurrection, and Paul answered each in turn. At the end he doesn't add one more rule.
He sets every rule under one. Watch, yes. Stand, yes.

teach.h: MY LOVE BE WITH YOU ALL.
teach.b: All of it with love. Then he picks up the pen himself: "The salutation of me Paul with mine own hand." And the very last words aren't a warning.
"My love be with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen."
A letter of hard corrections ends with love, sent to all of them, even the ones he argued with hardest.

how: Some churches take up a weekly collection for those in need, as Paul asks here, and some Christians keep 'let all your things be done with charity' as a motto for home or work.

games.q: what does “let all be done in love” mean?
o: keeping the peace by never disagreeing
everything done with love, not just done
giving money to every charity you can

games.q: let all be done in love — tap the pairs.

s: Paul ends his letter to Corinth with a final warning
the last words: my love be with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen.
charity in this verse means giving money to the poor
it's agape, love, the same word as chapter thirteen.
Paul writes the closing greeting with his own hand
the salutation of me Paul with mine own hand.

games.q: you're team captain after a season of arguments over playing time, rides and who's in charge. you get one minute at the end-of-season dinner. what fits Paul's closing?
o: thank everyone, name what you hope for next year, and say it with love.
settle every argument one last time, so nothing is left hanging.
skip the speech; love is something you show, never something you say.
games.why: after answering every quarrel, Paul closes with watch, stand fast, be strong, let all your things be done with charity, and my love be with you all.

practice: Open one hand. On each finger, count one thing someone did for you with love this week, however small: a ride, a saved plate, a text that came at the right time. When the hand is full, let it rest open on your knee.

wordCard.voice: Let all be done in love. Paul's closing call: every rule, gift and argument set under love.

orig.note: Greek: love. The King James renders it charity in 1 Corinthians 16:14, as in chapter 13.

carryVoice: The line to keep: all things with charity, the King James word for love. Week done.
